chunks: Al-Walid ibn Sabih narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said:
"Three people make du'a, but it is not answered for them"—or he said: "their du'a is returned to them."

A man who had abundant wealth, reaching thirty thousand or forty thousand, and he spent it away in its various avenues; then he says, "O Allah, provide for me," so Allah, the Exalted, says, "Did I not provide for you?"
And a man who refrains from seeking, then says, "O Allah, provide for me," so Allah, the Exalted, says, "Did I not make for you a way to seek?"
And a man who had a wife and said, "O Allah, separate between me and her," so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, "Did I not place that in your hands?"

key_terms.يَدْعُونَ: they make du'a or call upon Allah

ai.seo_question: Whose du'a is not answered according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that du'a is not accepted from those who neglect the means Allah has already placed at their disposal. It condemns wastefulness, abandoning lawful effort in seeking sustenance, and asking Allah to do what He has already entrusted to a person’s own agency in family matters.
